story.title: Female Athletes Criticize Sydney Sweeney's Nude Sports Betting Advertisement
story.summary: Sydney Sweeney is facing backlash from female athletes for her nude advertisement promoting a sports betting company. The ad has sparked criticism for its sexualized portrayal of women in sports, leading to widespread condemnation from various athletes worldwide.

explore_lenses.label: Why do athletes say the ad misrepresents women’s sports?
explore_lenses.title: The dispute is over the image of athleticism
explore_lenses.summary: Critics are not objecting simply to sexuality; they argue that a gambling ad uses a woman’s body as the product while sidelining the skill, work and physical reality of women’s competition.

claims.text: Olympic swimmer Ariarne Titmus called the campaign a “kick in the face” to women who have devoted themselves to sport, arguing that it monetizes women’s bodies rather than representing sport’s teamwork, dedication and excellence.

Boxer Skye Nicolson drew a distinction between athletes choosing to look sexy while doing sport and “use[ing] sex to sell ‘sport’,” framing the objection as one about the ad’s commercial use of sexualization.
Sprinter Amy Hunt used a post-race interview to contrast the ad’s glamour with elite sport’s training, sweat, injury-risk and bodily realities, including menstruation.

explore_lenses.label: What is Novig selling—and what is Sweeney’s role?
explore_lenses.title: A gambling-adjacent product with an investor spokesperson
explore_lenses.summary: The campaign promotes Novig’s sports prediction market, not a conventional sportsbook in the company’s description. Sweeney’s role goes beyond celebrity endorsement because Novig identifies her as both a strategic partner and equity holder.

claims.text: Novig says its users trade real-money contracts tied to sports outcomes; it describes the product as a CFTC-regulated prediction market rather than a state-licensed sportsbook.
Novig’s September 9 announcement says Sweeney joined the company as a strategic partner and equity holder while fronting its first national brand campaign.

Novig said the “Just Sports” campaign was intended to distinguish its sports-only platform from prediction markets covering politics, elections and other subjects; CEO Jacob Fortinsky said Sweeney helped create a message designed to be impossible to ignore.
Novig states that participation is limited to people 21 and older and markets the platform as a responsible-participation alternative within a growing prediction-market category.

explore_lenses.label: Will the campaign change after the backlash?
explore_lenses.title: The announced plan was to keep running it
explore_lenses.summary: As of September 14, Novig’s published plan was for the national campaign to run through football season, while Sweeney’s observable response was to share examples of athletes who had posed nude rather than issue a direct public statement addressing the athletes’ objections.

claims.text: Novig said its campaign would run across digital, social, online-video and out-of-home channels through football season, with further creative and activations planned for the fall.

After criticism emerged, Sweeney shared Instagram-story images of athletes including Serena Williams, Ronda Rousey, Sue Bird, Megan Rapinoe and Rob Gronkowski who had previously posed nude; Sky News characterized the posts as a defense of the ad.
Forecast: Based on Novig’s stated rollout schedule, the campaign was expected to remain visible during football season unless Novig or Sweeney chose to alter it.

story_report.summary: Sydney Sweeney’s nude advertisement for Novig, a sports prediction-market company, has drawn criticism from prominent female athletes who say its sexualized imagery conflicts with the work and achievement of women in sport. The backlash has focused attention on the commercial use of nudity in a campaign Novig says is part of its first national brand push, with Sweeney serving as a strategic partner and equity holder.

sections.heading: Athletes challenge campaign portrayal
sections.body: Olympic swimmer Ariarne Titmus called the campaign a “kick in the face” to women who have dedicated themselves to sport, arguing that it monetizes women’s bodies instead of reflecting teamwork, dedication and excellence. Boxer Skye Nicolson distinguished between athletes choosing to look sexy while competing and using sex to sell sport. Sprinter Amy Hunt likewise contrasted the advertisement’s glamour with the training, sweat, injury risk and menstruation involved in elite competition.

sections.heading: Novig describes sports-only marketplace
sections.body: Novig says users trade real-money contracts tied to sports outcomes and describes itself as a CFTC-regulated prediction market rather than a state-licensed sportsbook. In its September 9 announcement, the company said its “Just Sports” campaign was meant to differentiate its sports-focused platform from prediction markets involving politics, elections and other subjects. Novig says participation is limited to people 21 and older.

sections.heading: Campaign rollout remains scheduled
sections.body: Novig said the campaign would run across digital, social, online-video and out-of-home channels through football season, with additional creative work and activations planned for the fall. After criticism emerged, Sweeney posted Instagram-story images of athletes including Serena Williams, Ronda Rousey, Sue Bird, Megan Rapinoe and Rob Gronkowski who had previously posed nude; Sky News characterized the posts as a defense of the advertisement.

related_stories.summary: European leaders are gathering in Finland to address key issues related to the Arctic, including shipping routes, resource management, and security challenges posed by the increasing presence of Russia. The meeting comes as the region becomes more accessible due to melting ice, raising concerns about geopolitical tensions involving the US, China, and Russia.

related_stories.title: Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline Remains Closed Following Drone Attack
related_stories.summary: Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline remains shut after a drone attack attributed to Iranian-backed militias in Iraq. The attack occurred on September 10, 2026, and the pipeline is expected to be out of service for several weeks as repairs are undertaken. This disruption has contributed to rising oil prices globally.

related_stories.title: Gulf States Cancel Meeting with Iran Amid Houthi Attacks and Rising Tensions
related_stories.summary: Persian Gulf states have called off a planned meeting with Iran due to escalating tensions following new Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. The Houthis, backed by Iran, have intensified their offensive, prompting Saudi Arabia to express anger towards Tehran and seek additional military support from the United States. The situation has raised concerns over global oil supplies and the stability of the region.
